claims.claim: Michael Watkins' The First 90 Days (2003, updated 2013): the STARS model (start-up, turnaround, accelerated growth, realignment, sustaining success), five conversations with the boss (situation, expectations, resources, style, personal development), securing early wins and the trap of coming in with the answer.
claims.source: Shortform, SuperSummary and Mind Tools summaries found by search on 13 November 2026; the book itself was not checked.

concept_html:
People form their view of a new hire within weeks. Michael Watkins' The First 90 Days (2003, updated 2013) gives a plan for that window.

Diagnose the situation. Watkins' STARS model names five situations, each needing a different approach:

  • Start-up: building something new. Bring energy and set direction.
  • Turnaround: rescuing something failing. Act fast on the few things that matter.
  • Accelerated growth: scaling something that works. Add structure and process.
  • Realignment: something drifting into trouble that people do not yet see. Make the case for change.
  • Sustaining success: protecting what works. Learn before you change anything.

A talent data platform built from scattered HR extracts is usually a start-up, with parts that need realignment.

Five conversations with your manager. Hold them early, as separate topics:

  • Situation: do you both read the STARS situation the same way?
  • Expectations: what does success look like at 30, 60 and 90 days?
  • Resources: what people, budget and access will you have?
  • Style: how and how often do they want updates?
  • Personal development: which skills should you build in this role?

Learn before you change. Talk to the people who own the data before redesigning their processes. Arriving "with the answer" is a common trap.

Secure early wins. Pick small, visible results that matter to your manager's priorities and build trust, such as one data source mapped and validated with its owner. Agree them in the expectations conversation.

Record as you go. Write down each win, decision and lesson the week it happens. The app's Work log keeps them, tagged to your role plan phase, ready for your first review.

title: Your first 90 days in a new role
why_html: A new data lead spent their first month redesigning the HR data model without talking to the payroll team. The payroll lead, whose reports depended on the old fields, objected at the first steering group, and the design stalled for six weeks. A listening tour in week one would have surfaced the dependency and turned the payroll lead into an early ally.
